description: A minimal browser-based Skyline dice game, hosted free on GitHub Pages, with one player hosting a room and playing while other devices on the same local network join and receive each round's shared dice roll.

questions.question: Which language should the web game use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing to help keep multiplayer game state and UI changes reliable.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Keeps a small browser game straightforward, with no compile-time type checking.

questions.rationale: TypeScript is a sensible default for coordinating shared game state across devices.

questions.question: What frontend framework or approach would you prefer?

options.label: Plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
options.description: Minimal dependencies and a small static site that can be published directly with GitHub Pages.

options.label: React
options.description: A component-based approach with a broad ecosystem.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A lightweight component framework with approachable conventions.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: A component framework that compiles to a small browser bundle.

questions.rationale: A minimal static game is a natural fit for a small vanilla frontend and GitHub Pages.

questions.question: What rules and MVP game flow should the Skyline game implement? Please describe the version of Skyline you mean (or provide/link the rules), including how turns and rounds work, what each dice roll does, how a winner is determined, and any must-have screens or controls.
questions.rationale: The game name alone does not establish which ruleset or scoring flow to implement.

questions.question: How should devices connect while keeping GitHub Pages as the free static UI host? A static GitHub Pages site cannot itself accept LAN connections or act as a room server.
questions.recommendedChoice: Browser-to-browser WebRTC with host-controlled room state and QR/manual pairing

options.label: Browser-to-browser WebRTC with host-controlled room state and QR/manual pairing
options.description: The host's browser creates and controls the room, plays too, and broadcasts rolls directly to guests. The GitHub Pages site stays static and free; devices need a pairing/signaling step, and connectivity depends on browser/network support.

options.label: Run a small room server on the host device
options.description: Guests join the host device's LAN address, and the host can also play. GitHub Pages can remain the public static UI, but the host must start/install a local server and allow LAN access.

options.label: Use an online relay/room service
options.description: Devices join through a hosted signaling or realtime service while the UI remains on GitHub Pages. This is easiest to join, but adds an external dependency, may require internet access, and free-tier terms/limits can change.

questions.rationale: The connection model determines whether this can remain a static, backend-free GitHub Pages app or needs a local/hosted room service.

questions.question: What is the expected maximum number of players/devices in a room, and should the host create/join rooms with a room code, QR code, or a simple shareable link?
questions.rationale: Room size and joining experience shape the simplest reliable multiplayer implementation.

questions.question: Should the game save anything between sessions, such as player names, scores, or match history?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Keep game state in the active room/session only; nothing is persisted.

options.label: Browser local storage
options.description: Save preferences or local history on each device; this does not synchronize room state between devices.

questions.rationale: No persistent storage was requested; each round's shared roll is live room state rather than a saved record.

questions.question: Should players sign in to use game features, or should anyone with the room invitation be able to join?

options.label: No
options.description: No sign-in; players join an active room using its invitation.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Players must sign in before using game features.

questions.rationale: A minimal casual game does not need accounts unless you want account-based features.
